summary.title: ArtisanMarket Client Threat Model
summary.description: Plan-stage threat model (Section 4.3.1) for the ArtisanMarket storefront SPA (React 18, Vite 7, TypeScript; Redux Toolkit and TanStack Query; nginx static host on Kubernetes; ArtisanMarket API over HTTPS and Socket.IO; Stripe.js, ImageKit, Plaid Link). Covers browsing and search, registration and login, cart and checkout, vendor dashboards and product reviews. Everything shipped in the bundle is public: the SPA is a client of the trust boundary, never an enforcer of it; all authorisation decisions belong to the API.

data.name: Build env (VITE_* variables)
data.description: Build-time environment variables inlined into the public bundle by Vite.

threats.title: Secret placed in a public build variable
threats.description: Every import.meta.env.VITE_* value is inlined into the public bundle. A private key placed in one is world-readable.
threats.mitigation: Only publishable values are used: VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, VITE_IMAGEKIT_PUBLIC_KEY, VITE_API_URL, VITE_SOCKET_URL. Gitleaks gate at Code stage. Secret keys must stay server-side.

data.name: CI pipeline
data.description: GitHub Actions pipeline (.github/workflows/pipeline.yml) running the Plan, Code, Build, Staging, Deploy and Monitor gates.

data.name: Static host (nginx)
data.description: nginx container serving the static bundle and header policy, deployed with the k8s/ manifests.

threats.title: Vulnerable or over-privileged serving image
threats.description: A serving image or deployment manifest could carry known CVEs or run as root (Tampering / Denial of service).
threats.mitigation: Trivy image scan and Checkov at Build stage. The first image scan found 40 findings (2 CRITICAL) from nginx:1.27-alpine pinning Alpine 3.21.3; pinned forward to nginx:1.31.6-alpine and patched libexpat (CVE-2026-93990) and pcre2 (CVE-2026-103111, published after the image had passed every gate), now clean at CRITICAL/HIGH. Checkov: 89 checks pass, with one documented exception (CKV_K8S_43 image digest).

data.name: Shopper / vendor
data.description: Visitor using a browser: browsing, search, registration and login, cart and checkout, vendor dashboards, reviews.

data.name: React SPA
data.description: React 18 single-page application (Vite 7, TypeScript) executing in the visitor's browser. Fully attacker-inspectable; a client of the trust boundary, never an enforcer of it.

threats.title: Attacker-supplied content rendered as HTML
threats.description: Attacker-supplied content (review bodies, shop descriptions) rendered as raw HTML would execute as script. This is the delivery path for T1 and also enables elevation of privilege within the user's session.
threats.mitigation: No dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML assignment anywhere in src/; React escapes by default. Code-stage ESLint and SonarQube rules block both sinks. Any future use is a blocking review item.

threats.title: Client-side route guards mistaken for access control
threats.description: Hiding vendor or admin routes in the SPA is presentation only; the bundle can be read and any route reached directly.
threats.mitigation: Not a client-side control: every privileged action is authorised server-side by the ArtisanMarket API. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for a mitigation.

data.name: Redux store
data.description: Redux Toolkit (src/store/) and TanStack Query server state, in memory.

data.name: SW cache
data.description: Workbox precache created by vite-plugin-pwa.

threats.title: Authenticated responses persisted in service worker cache
threats.description: vite-plugin-pwa with registerType 'autoUpdate' and a broad globPatterns cache could persist authenticated responses in the browser cache across sessions.
threats.mitigation: Cache only static build assets; never add API responses to precache. No automated gate covers this, so it is verified manually on each Workbox config change.

data.name: localStorage (session token)
data.description: Browser storage holding the JWT issued by the API; written at three call sites in src/store/slices/authSlice.ts.

threats.title: Session token readable by any script on the origin
threats.description: The JWT is held in localStorage, which is readable by any script running on the origin. A single XSS flaw, in first-party code or any dependency, exfiltrates a full session.
threats.mitigation: Risk formally accepted for this iteration. Rationale: the API issues bearer tokens; moving to an HttpOnly cookie is a cross-repo change touching login, authMiddleware, CORS credentials and every authenticated request path, with a real risk of breaking authentication. Compensating control: T2 keeps every HTML sink closed (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML in src/, blocked by the Code-stage ruleset). ESLint blocks any new credential write to browser storage; the three existing call sites in src/store/slices/authSlice.ts carry scoped, justified eslint-disable-next-line exceptions. Remediation path: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie issued by the API; remove all localStorage token access and the three exceptions. Review when auth is next modified.

threats.title: Compromised or vulnerable dependency
threats.description: The bundle inlines dependency code and ships it to every visitor, so a compromised or vulnerable package executes in the user's browser. A compromised build tool can affect the bundle even though it never ships.
threats.mitigation: SCA gates on the full dependency tree, both blocking: npm audit on every branch, run through scripts/audit-gate.mjs, which allows a named advisory to be accepted only with a reason and a review date (.audit-allowlist.json); and a Trivy dependency scan at Build stage (staging and main). Snyk is wired in as an optional step but is not configured and does not run. Findings reduced from 36 (1 critical, 26 high, 7 moderate) to 2 moderates (react-router, react-router-dom) after upgrading to Vite 7. The earlier --omit=dev scoping has been reverted, because a compromised build tool can affect the bundle even though it never ships.

threats.title: Missing security response headers
threats.description: Without CSP, X-Frame-Options and HSTS, the SPA is exposed to clickjacking and script injection that a header policy would blunt (Tampering / Information disclosure).
threats.mitigation: Header policy is configured in nginx.conf inside the serving image. Not yet verified: the Staging DAST gate (OWASP ZAP baseline) scans vite preview on port 4173, which serves no headers. Pointing DAST at a container built from the production image would close this; until then the ZAP exceptions in .zap/rules.tsv remain.

threats.title: Card data reaching ArtisanMarket systems
threats.description: Card data must never reach ArtisanMarket servers or the Redux store (Repudiation / Information disclosure).
threats.mitigation: Stripe Elements keeps card entry inside a Stripe-hosted iframe, holding the app in PCI DSS SAQ-A scope. Any move to raw card fields changes that materially.
